scenario: First bootstrap of folders that already hold notes
prompt: Set up my PKA here. I'm Sam, an engineering manager. I already have a folder structure, and I like short, direct answers.
followups: The map looks right. Completed projects archive to knowledge/archived/. Go ahead and write everything.
expect: scans the folder structure with tool calls before asking its first question; presents a draft Repo Map in which knowledge/leadership is tagged meeting-home and knowledge/personnel is tagged people-home; names an archive destination or asks for one; keeps the interview to name or profile, autonomy level and the Repo Map (never more than five questions in total); recommends markdown-only storage because the knowledge folders hold fewer than 300 indexable files, and creates no .pka/knowledge.db; installs the toolkit by running the plugin's `pka-tools install --workspace .`, not by writing files under .pka/bin/ itself; writes CLAUDE.md with a `## Repo Map` table, a `## Archive Destination` section and the note that transcripts in team-inbox/ are held for pka-meetings; creates .pka/roles/ with orchestrator.md, researcher.md, librarian.md, roster.md and _obsidian.md; creates .pka/session-log.md with a bootstrap entry, .pka/owner-profile.md and .pka/decision-log.md; writes .pkaignore and creates owner-inbox/ and team-inbox/; moves, renames or deletes nothing under knowledge/, projects/ or meeting-notes/; shows what `pka-tools lint schedule` prints and says nothing was installed; runs no git command

scenario: Bootstrap in an empty folder: infrastructure always, one starter layout on offer
prompt: Bootstrap PKA in this empty folder. I'm Sam, a product lead; keep things brief.
expect: treats the folder as a fresh setup with nothing to map; offers one starter layout (knowledge/ with meetings/ and personnel/ inside it, projects/, and knowledge/archive/ as the archive destination), the user's own folder names, or none; creates no content folder before the user answers that offer; keeps the interview to name or profile, autonomy level and the layout question; creates the infrastructure whatever the answer: .pkaignore, .pka/ with the toolkit installed by the plugin's `pka-tools install --workspace .`, the role files and the session log, CLAUDE.md, owner-inbox/ and team-inbox/; after the yes the folders knowledge/, knowledge/meetings/, knowledge/personnel/, knowledge/archive/ and projects/ exist and nothing is created inside them; the Repo Map in CLAUDE.md has those five rows, with meeting-home on knowledge/meetings/ and people-home on knowledge/personnel/; storage mode is Markdown-only and there is no .pka/knowledge.db; writes a bootstrap entry to .pka/session-log.md; runs no git command

scenario: Bootstrap asked for from inside a project workspace
expect: finds the .pka/ folder in a parent directory by walking up from the current folder; refuses to bootstrap from inside the project workspace; gives the path of the PKA root and says to run the bootstrap from there; creates or changes no file

scenario: A CLAUDE.md that is not PKA's, and no .pka/

text: Use British spelling. Never touch the drafts folder.

prompt: Set up PKA in this folder.
followups: It's unrelated, just some old instructions. I'm Sam, an engineer. Ask before destructive actions.
The map is right, archive to knowledge/archived/. Go ahead.
expect: the first reply notices the CLAUDE.md with no PKA infrastructure beside it and asks whether it is an existing PKA or an unrelated file; CLAUDE.md is not overwritten or edited before the user answers that question; before replacing CLAUDE.md it shows the difference between the old and the new content and asks for confirmation; CLAUDE.md still holds its original text when the run ends, because that confirmation was never given

scenario: Project transition stops for approval of the summary, even hands-off
expect: takes the archive destination from CLAUDE.md (knowledge/archived/); writes a project summary draft to owner-inbox/orion-summary-draft.md; stops and asks the user to review and approve the summary before anything is moved, although the autonomy level is hands-off; projects/orion is still in place and nothing under knowledge/ has changed when the run ends; runs no git command

scenario: R5 — After approval the project moves and the links that pointed at it follow

text: Project workspace. Wrapped up in October.

followups: The summary is approved and there is nothing to clean up. Go ahead with the move.
expect: the first reply writes the summary draft to owner-inbox/ and pauses for approval before moving anything; after approval moves the folder to knowledge/archived/lyra with mv, not with git mv and not by rewriting files one at a time; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools pointers rename projects/lyra knowledge/archived/lyra --prefix --notes` and reports how many links were rewritten; the wikilinks in knowledge/AI/lyra-overview.md, knowledge/lab-notebook/2026-10-05.md and knowledge/AI/_MOC.md no longer point at projects/lyra; searches for what still mentions the old path and tells the user what is left to fix by hand, or that nothing is; copies the approved summary into the moved folder as project-summary.md; adds a row for knowledge/archived/lyra/ to the Repo Map in CLAUDE.md, Priority Reference and Status archived, leaving the rows for projects/ and knowledge/archived/ as they were; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools index` only after that row is in the Repo Map; the moved project's files are in the index afterwards (the index command reports them added, or `status` lists the folder under index roots); appends a session-log entry and adds an entry to .pka/decision-log.md; runs neither graduate.sh nor any git command, and says the move is left for the user to commit

scenario: R6 — The project being transitioned is its own repository

text: Project workspace with its own history.

followups: The summary is approved, nothing to clean up, go ahead.
expect: stops before moving and asks about the repository at projects/lyra/.git; explains that a plain move would carry the project's repository into the destination and that PKA no longer manages nested repositories; lays out the choice between moving .git aside first and letting it travel with the folder; projects/lyra and projects/lyra/.git are unchanged when the run ends; runs no git command and no graduate.sh

scenario: Which projects are winding down
prompt: What projects haven't had activity recently?
expect: checks the project workspaces (folders with their own CLAUDE.md) with tool calls rather than answering from memory; names projects/orion as having had no activity for more than 60 days; does not flag projects/lyra; gives the last-activity date or age of what it flags; moves, archives and edits nothing

scenario: Adding a role to the team
prompt: Add a data analyst to my team.
expect: writes a competency brief to owner-inbox/research-data-analyst-{{today}}.md; writes .pka/roles/data-analyst.md with role frontmatter and the standard sections (Purpose, Specialty, Key Competencies, Working Style, Output Conventions, Invocation); adds the role to .pka/roles/roster.md; shows the definition to the user and asks for confirmation; appends a session-log entry

scenario: S3 — Obsidian bootstrap of a vault with no MOCs and no person pages
expect: seeds .pka/roles/_obsidian.md because it is missing; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools obsidian bootstrap --dry-run` and shows the counts before the real run; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools obsidian bootstrap`; makes no Write or Edit call on a file under knowledge/ (the command does the retrofit); a _MOC.md now exists in knowledge/AI/ and knowledge/leadership/ and an index.md in every person folder; relays the counts the command printed (MOC stubs created, person indexes created, files given frontmatter, total touched); lists the skipped files by path (the note with malformed frontmatter and the one that is not UTF-8); says nothing was committed and the changes are the user's to review; runs no git command

scenario: S4 — Obsidian bootstrap run twice
expect: the first run applies the retrofit with `.pka/bin/pka-tools obsidian bootstrap`; the second run reports nothing new: zero created and zero files touched, everything already present; says so to the user instead of presenting the second run as having changed something; runs no git command on either run

scenario: S5 and S6 — Obsidian bootstrap with the owner's own MOC and person page, and a note with broken frontmatter
prompt: Run bootstrap obsidian. I wrote the MOC in AI/ and Priya's index page myself.
expect: knowledge/AI/_MOC.md, knowledge/leadership/_MOC.md and knowledge/personnel/priya/index.md are not among the changed files; tells the user the existing MOCs and person page were left alone (already present); the missing pieces are still created, for example an index.md for robin-smith; `knowledge/leadership/2026-05-06-budget review.md` is reported by path as skipped for malformed frontmatter and is not among the changed files; does not try to repair the malformed frontmatter; the retrofit carries on past the skipped file (other notes gain frontmatter)

scenario: S11 — A researcher brief saved inside an Obsidian vault
prompt: @researcher: from what is already in my notes, write a short brief on where we stand with AI adoption and save it in knowledge/AI/.
expect: saves a new brief under knowledge/AI/; its frontmatter has `type: brief`, a `date`, a `related` list and `tags` that include research and ai; `related` either links the existing brief as a wikilink ([[AI/ai-adoption-research]]) or is an empty list, and names no file that does not exist; references to vault files in the body are [[wikilinks]]; the brief has Sources, Confidence (or an equivalent) and Open Questions sections; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools post-route` on the saved brief; runs no git command

scenario: S11 — The same brief when there is no Obsidian vault
prompt: @researcher: from what is already in my notes, write a short brief on where we stand with AI adoption and save it in knowledge/AI/.
expect: saves a new brief under knowledge/AI/; the brief has no YAML frontmatter; the brief contains no [[wikilinks]], its references are plain markdown links or paths; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools post-route` on the saved brief; runs no git command

scenario: R1 — 'Bootstrap git' names a removed target
prompt: Bootstrap git. I want the hybrid monorepo with a repo per project.
expect: says the git / hybrid-monorepo target was removed; says PKA no longer sets up nested repositories, commits or pushes; says a workspace is kept in one ordinary repository (or none) that the user commits themselves; runs no git command, creates no .meta and neither looks for nor runs init_project_repos.sh; offers the bootstraps that do exist (base setup, obsidian, upgrade)

scenario: R2 — Upgrade of a pre-1.7 workspace that has the nested-repository layout

text: # pushes every nested repository (from an earlier release)
# graduates a project into knowledge/ (from an earlier release)

expect: runs the plugin's installer (`pka-tools install --workspace .`) before the role upgrade; relays that push-all.sh and graduate.sh were left in place and are no longer maintained; neither deletes nor edits .meta, .gitignore, any .git folder, .pka/push-all.sh, .pka/graduate.sh or .pka/graduate-backups/; runs `python3 .pka/upgrade-roles.py --workspace` and relays its Obsolete list (_git-protocol.md, the Commit/push protocol sections, the orchestrator's push sections); asks once before running --refresh and says that it removes the obsolete sections that were never edited; passes neither --refresh nor --refresh-section before the user answers; tells the user that nothing is committed or pushed for them any more; runs no git command

scenario: R3 — An obsolete section the owner had edited survives the refresh

steps.old: When the orchestrator's session-start detection reports `hybrid_monorepo_present` true:
steps.new: Sam's rule: when the orchestrator's session-start detection reports `hybrid_monorepo_present` true, and only on weekdays:

followups: Yes, go ahead with the refresh.
expect: the first reply relays that researcher.md's Commit/push protocol section is customised and was left alone; after the yes it runs upgrade-roles.py with --refresh and without --refresh-section; reports that the customised section was kept; says the kept section still tells the researcher to commit and that this must not be followed, because nothing commits any more; offers to show the difference (--diff) and to remove that section only on an explicit yes for it; .pka/roles/researcher.md still contains the line beginning `Sam's rule:` when the run ends

scenario: Upgrade of a workspace whose role files pin a model
expect: runs the plugin's installer and then `python3 .pka/upgrade-roles.py --workspace`; relays the helper's Pinned models list: orchestrator.md, researcher.md and librarian.md each have a `model:` line; says roles no longer pin a model and that the line can be removed so the role follows the session's model; offers to remove the lines and removes none without a yes: the frontmatter of the three role files is unchanged when the run ends; relays the sections the helper added, among them `Owner profile and decision log` in all three role files and `Answering and delegating` in the orchestrator; asks before running --refresh

scenario: R4 — Asked to push
expect: runs no git push, no push-all.sh and no `meta git push` (no git command at all); says PKA no longer pushes or commits; says pushing is the user's to do

scenario: L5 — Session start with a lint report from three days ago that has findings
expect: runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools lint latest`, with or without --json; the greeting has one line that gives the report's date ({{today-3}}), the number of findings `lint latest` returned and the report's path (owner-inbox/librarian-lint-{{today-3}}.md); runs no lint (no `pka-tools lint` other than `lint latest`); neither lists the individual findings nor acts on them

scenario: L6 — Session start when the newest lint report is twenty days old
expect: greets the user with the session-start items (open threads, inbox, lifecycle flags) it found by tool calls; the greeting has no line about a health check or lint report; runs no lint (no `pka-tools lint` other than `lint latest`)

scenario: A lookup is answered by the orchestrator itself, not delegated
prompt: What did the SLT decide about the vendor at the end of April?
expect: answers the question itself from the notes: the vendor decision was deferred, per knowledge/leadership/2026-04-29-slt-meeting.md; names that file as the source; does not hand the lookup to @researcher or @librarian, and writes no brief or report for it; changes no file
